module_title: Bhakti and Sufi Movements - Maharashtra Dharma, Orthodox Orders, and Textual Analysis
introduction: At this advanced level, we will deeply analyze the profound impact of the 'Varkari' sect in Maharashtra, the verses of various saints included in the Guru Granth Sahib, the orthodox Sufi orders (like Naqshbandi) during the Later Mughal period, and their ideological clashes with rulers.

core_concepts.title: Maharashtra Dharma (Varkari Sect)
core_concepts.description: The worship of Lord Vitthal (Vithoba) of Pandharpur became popular in Maharashtra. Saints like Jñāneśvar, Namdev, Eknath, and Tukaram wrote 'Abhangas' in Marathi and struck a heavy blow against the caste system.

core_concepts.title: Saints' Verses in Guru Granth Sahib
core_concepts.description: The fifth Sikh Guru, 'Arjan Dev', compiled the 'Adi Granth'. It contains not only the hymns of Sikh Gurus but also the verses of Bhakti saints like Kabir, Namdev, Ravidas (Raidas), and the Sufi saint Baba Farid.

core_concepts.title: Naqshbandi Order
core_concepts.description: This was the most orthodox (conservative) Sufi order. Its prominent saint, 'Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi', strongly opposed Akbar's liberal religious policies (Din-i-Ilahi) and Shias.

core_concepts.title: Qadiri Order and Dara Shikoh
core_concepts.description: Saint 'Mian Mir' (who laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple) was a famous figure of this order. Shah Jahan's eldest son, 'Dara Shikoh', was a devoted follower of the Qadiri Silsila.

core_concepts.title: Other Philosophies of Vedanta
core_concepts.description: Madhvacharya's 'Dvaitavada' (Dualism - asserting that the soul and God are completely different entities) and Vallabhacharya's 'Shuddhadvaita' (Pure Non-dualism - associated with Pushtimarg).

important_entities.name: Namdev
important_entities.significance: Initially a bandit, his Marathi compositions became highly popular in North India and were later included in the 'Guru Granth Sahib'.

important_entities.name: Dara Shikoh
important_entities.significance: He translated 52 Upanishads into Persian under the title 'Sirr-i-Akbar' (The Great Secret) and authored 'Majma-ul-Bahrain' (The Mingling of Two Oceans - Hinduism and Islam).

important_entities.name: Baba Farid (Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar)
important_entities.significance: He spread Sufism in Punjab. His teachings were highly respected and found a place in the holy scripture of the Sikhs.

important_entities.name: Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi
important_entities.significance: He was called 'Mujaddid Alf Thani' (Reformer of the second millennium); Emperor Jahangir briefly imprisoned him.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because of Dara Shikoh's liberal mindset, students often assume he belonged to the 'Chishti' order. However, Dara Shikoh was actually a follower of the 'Qadiri' order.
There were two main sects in Maharashtra: 'Varkari' (Devotees of Vithoba, peaceful approach, e.g., Tukaram) and 'Dharkari' (Devotees of Ram, militant/active approach, e.g., Shivaji's guru Ramdas).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember the chronological order: Gyan(eshwar) -> N(amdev) -> Ek(nath) -> Tukka(ram).

exam_strategy_tips: In exams like UPSC, expect analytical, statement-based questions regarding which specific saints' verses are included (or not included) in the 'Guru Granth Sahib'.
Study Dara Shikoh's literary works and the subtle differences between the various 'Advaita' (Non-dual) philosophies deeply.
